metric_model: CHAOSS AI Alignment - Community Governed Use

scope.note: Scoring confined to the files named on the command line; 'no' means not addressed in those files.

domains.scope_or_volume_limits: Applies to all official Jellyfin projects; PRs must be concise/focused and broken into multiple small, manageable commits; features/refactors require in-depth understanding
domains.accountability_wording: you are responsible for what you commit

evidence.quote: you are responsible for what you commit
You must review the output and be able to explain in the PR body ... what is being changed and why.
do not just let an LLM loose on the codebase with a vague vibe prompt and then commit the results as-is
The final discretion always lies with the reviewers.

domains.reasoning: The policy explicitly and extensively addresses AI-assisted code contributions: it requires human review/understanding, testing, concise scoped PRs, and states the contributor bears responsibility for what is committed, with reviewers holding final discretion.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of meeting/notetaker bots or recorded discussion at all
domains.reasoning: The document never discusses recording, transcription, or bots attending meetings/discussions.

domains.suggested_improvement: no rule on AI use for the project's own docs, blogs, or design assets
domains.reasoning: The only mention of 'docs' appears in the section about third-party community-shared tools/clients ('If you used an LLM for secondary assistance (e.g. docs, formatting, etc.) in an obvious way, we would err towards disclosure as well'), which concerns other people's external projects, not the project's own documentation, blog posts, or design assets. No rule addresses AI use in producing Jellyfin's own content.

domains.suggested_improvement: no rule on AI use in taking moderation actions
domains.reasoning: The document states human moderators will not police third-party projects line-by-line for LLM origin ('we, the moderators, are not going to play LLM police'), but this describes human moderator effort/discretion, not any AI tool being used to perform moderation actions, so the domain itself is unaddressed.

domains.suggested_improvement: no statement on whether AI may be used to review contributions
domains.reasoning: The policy discusses human reviewers having final discretion and contributors reviewing their own LLM output, but nowhere addresses whether AI tools themselves may be used to review PRs/issues/code.

evidence.quote: do not just let an LLM loose on the codebase with a vague vibe prompt and then commit the results as-is

domains.suggested_improvement: no rule on agents acting on the repository independently
domains.reasoning: The 'golden rule' against 'vibe coding' warns against low-effort, unsupervised LLM-driven changes, but describes a human still submitting/committing the code rather than an autonomous agent independently interacting with the repository (e.g., opening PRs, commenting, or merging on its own). No such agentic/autonomous scenario is named, so this is a restrictive lean rather than an addressed rule for this domain.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of energy, water, or carbon footprint concerns
domains.reasoning: No text in the document discusses environmental cost of AI tools.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of server load or hardware/financing strain
domains.reasoning: No text addresses server load, hosting costs, or hardware financing related to AI.

domains.suggested_improvement: no statement on use of project's own data/content for model training
domains.reasoning: The document discusses copyright/attribution obligations for code contributors (respecting licenses, crediting contributors) but never addresses whether Jellyfin's own user data, issues, discussions, or content may be used to train AI models.

unscoped_statements.quote: These rules apply to all of our official projects and community spaces.

consent_policy_specificity.overall_posture: Jellyfin's policy is highly specific and restrictive about AI use in code contributions and direct textual communication (issues/PRs/comments/forum posts), requiring human understanding, review, and disclosure/attribution in specific cases, but it is entirely silent on notetaker bots, the project's own content/documentation production, AI-assisted moderation, AI-assisted review, autonomous agentic action, environmental impact, infrastructure strain, and use of the project's own data for training.

awaiting_implementation.specific_tools_in_use: Awaiting implementation: named-product detection beyond known file signatures
awaiting_implementation.ai_tool_owner: Awaiting implementation: ownership and data control
awaiting_implementation.environmental_footprint: Awaiting implementation: model/system card and ESG disclosure
awaiting_implementation.proportionality: Awaiting implementation: resource use relative to contributor count (needs platform usage data)

use_composition_partial.note: Detection only. Absence of signal is not absence of use.

policy_change.blocker: Draft classifier not wired in or validated against hand-graded history. Repo.history() and Repo.commit_patch() supply the diffs.

use_compliance.blocker: Derived metric. Requires disclosed-use data (Use Composition) checked against the specificity grid. Composition is only partially detectable, so the comparison is not yet sound.

misuse.blocker: Not automatable. CHAOSS marks the core signals unknown: text-based AI detectors are unreliable, and license-laundering and wrongful-accusation incidents need maintainer self-report.
